name: PyramidKV: Dynamic KV Cache Compression based on Pyramidal Information Funneling
problem: Every KV-cache compression method allocates the SAME budget to every layer, which contradicts how transformers actually route information through depth.
mechanism: The observation is Pyramidal Information Funneling: attention is scattered and diffuse in LOWER layers, progressively consolidates into specific contexts in middle layers, and focuses on a few critical tokens (massive activations / attention sinks) in HIGHER layers. PyramidKV therefore allocates a PYRAMIDAL budget - more cache in lower layers, less in higher ones - rather than a uniform one.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract), reported as quality-at-budget rather than as a speedup: matches full-KV-cache performance while retaining only 12% of the KV cache (LongBench); in memory-focused settings retaining 0.7% of the KV cache it beats other compression methods by up to 20.5 absolute accuracy points on TREC; and with just 128 retained KV entries LLAMA-3-70B reaches 100.0 accuracy on needle-in-a-haystack. The 12%-of-cache figure is a MEMORY reduction with a quality floor - the serving consequence is batch size, not tok/s.
